claims.supporting_quote: Serum levels of 25(OH)D were determined significantly lower in migraine patients (n=952) in comparison with healthy controls (n=8013) [eight studies, PQ<0.1, I2=94%, RE model MD=-4.11, 95% CI=(-6.48, -1.74)].
Migraine patients had significantly lower mean (SD) of serum VitD (30 (16) ng/mL) than healthy subjects (43 (19) ng/mL) (P < .001).
Compared with controls, women with migraine had lower serum 25(OH)D and calcium levels (p ≤ 0.001)

claims.symptoms: High-frequency episodic migraine or chronic migraine (HF/CM)
claims.supporting_quote: Mean 25(OH)D levels in females with HF/CM (median [interquartile range] 19.0 [13.0-24.5] ng/mL) were below the values considered for insufficiency or deficiency and significantly lower than controls (25.0 [19-29.8] ng/mL; p < 0.0001)

The median serum 25(OH)D was 56 nmol/L (IQR 41, 69) in children with headaches and 70 nmol/L (IQR 50, 95) in children with epilepsy. Vitamin D insufficiency was present in 42% of children with headaches and 25% of children with epilepsy
No significant association was found between migraine and serum 25(OH)D. Non-migraine headache was associated with low levels of serum 25(OH)D.
